Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2899 of 2009
Judgment:

The appellant-insurance company has preferred this appeal aggrieved by the award dated 14.11.2008 in M.V.O.P.No.1689 of 2006 passed by the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge for the Trial of JHCBBC-cum-Additional Family Court-cum-XXIII Additional Chief Judge at Hyderabad.

entities.text: JHCBBC-cum-Additional Family Court-cum-XXIII Additional Chief Judge at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Mr. K.S.N. Murthy, learned Standing Counsel for the appellant-insurance company and Mr. Chandrashekar Reddy Gopireddy, learned Counsel for the respondents and perused the entire material on record.
3.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of death of deceased in the motor vehicle accident that took place on 26.02.2006.

It is the case of the claimants that on 26.02.2006, when the deceased was going on his motorcycle from Nagaram to Shamshabad,
one auto rickshaw driven by its driver in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed his motorcycle, due to which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and thereafter succumbed to the injuries.

It is their further case that the deceased was earning an amount of Rs.6000/- per month and the Court below considering the evidence on record has come to the conclusion that the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.3,27,000/- towards compensation but however restricted the same to Rs.3,00,000/-.
4.

The appellant-insurance company is before this court stating that they are not liable to pay the compensation as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving license at the time of the accident.

To buttress the said submission, it is submitted that as per the FIR and charge sheet,
the crime is registered under Section 3 and 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

It is further stated that when the driver is not having a valid driving license and also as there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, the appellant- insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
5. Learned Counsel appearing for the claimants submits that though the Court below has held that the claimants are entitled for Rs.3,27,000/-, however restricted the same to Rs.3,00,000/-.
He submits that the future prospects were not considered by the Court below.

Though they have not preferred any separate appeal, the Act being a beneficial legislation, he submits that this Court may consider the appeal on merits and also on quantum and may grant the appropriate compensation.

sentences.text:
In response to that learned Standing Counsel for appellant-insurance company submits that when the appellant- insurance company is on questioning the liability and when no appeal is preferred by the claimants and also when the whole of compensation amount claimed by them was awarded by the Court below, it cannot be termed that he is aggrieved by the award and the claimants are not entitled for any enhancement in their appeal.
7.

Firstly, coming to the enhancement that is sought by the claimants in the appeal filed by the appellant-insurance company, no doubt, in catena of the cases, this Court as well as the Apex Court has held that the Act being a beneficial legislation, it should be the endeavour of the Courts to see that the claimants are being paid a just and reasonable compensation and in case where there is no appeal preferred by the claimants, still the Courts are considering their case for enhancement of the compensation as the Act being a beneficial legislation.

This Court has passed several orders wherein whenever the insurance company is before this court questioning the quantum without there being any appeal preferred by the claimants, this Court is considering the case of the claimants and in the appeal of the insurance company also, whenever it is required in the facts of the case, this Court is enhancing the compensation.

But whenever the insurance company is before this Court only on the liability then this Court is not at all going into the aspect of quantum, in those cases, and is refusing to entertain the claim of the claimants for enhancement now, in this case where the claim of compensation is Rs.3,00,000/- and the Court below has already awarded the said amount.
When there is no appeal preferred by the claimants and insurance company preferred this appeal only on liability, this Court is not inclined to go into the said question of enhancement.

8. Coming to the case of the appellant-insurance company that there was no valid driving license and crime is registered under section 3 and 181 of the Motor Vehicles act 1988 and that itself shows that driver of the vehicle was not having a valid driving license.
The Court below ought not to have fastened the liability on the appellant-insurance company.

9. As per the law laid down in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh1, when appellant-insurance company is claiming that there is violation of the policy conditions and the driver of the vehicle was not having a valid driving license, the 2004(3) SCC 297 burden lies on them to prove the same by examining the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In this case, the appellant-insurance company except relying on the charge sheet and FIR, has not adduced any evidence to prove the same.
The Court below has rightly held that the appellant-insurance company and the owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, this Court do not find any grounds to interfere with the award passed by the Court below.
11. Accordingly, the appeal of the appellant-insurance company is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J Date: 18.07.2023 myk M/S Iffcotokio General Insurance Co. ... vs Rajamani And 3 Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81584871/
